simple.meaning: גָּהָה (gâhâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to remove (a bandage from a wound, i.e. heal it).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Hosea, beginning at Hosea 5:13. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּהָה (H1455) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.

definitions.full: H1455. gahah [ גָּהָה ] verb depart , i.e. be cured, healed (subject wound) (compare Aramaic be freed (from guilt, pain, disease, etc.), Aph`el set free , also become free ) מָזוֺר מִכֶּם ולאיִֿגְהֶה Hosea 5:13 .
